title.narrative: Improving Services for Victims of Gender Based and Domestic Violence

description.narrative: "The Development Objective for this project is to support the Republic of Kiribati to improve access to services in favor of women victims of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and in particular Domestic Violence. The Project has three components: 1) Workshop and Diagnostic Study on Services Available for Victims of Domestic Violence; 2) Pilot Subproject to address core capacity by frontline responders in particular focused on standardized provision of services to victims of GBV and DV; and 3) Strengthening Reporting, Data Collection and Monitoring of GBV within Service Providers. High levels of domestic violence across the Pacific undermine development. Kiribati reports some of the highest rates of gender violence in the world. Indeed, 68% of women (two out of every three women) between the ages of 15 and 49 years reported experiencing physical or sexual violence, or both, by an intimate partner. Violence against women significantly and negatively affects not only their health and well-being, and agency, but also affects the public health system, business, and children's development, education, and nutrition levels. Women who have experienced intimate partner violence in Kiribati are seven times more likely to have children who are also abused than those who have not experienced partner violence. Children exposed to domestic violence are more likely to later perpetrate or experience domestic violence as adults, endangering the health, nutrition and education of future generations. Police forces are grappling with rising cases of GBV and DV but still believe these are ""family issues"". The overwhelming majority of abused women (78% of them) reported that they had never sought help from formal services (health, legal advice or shelter services) or from people in positions of authority (police, non government organizations, religious or local leaders). This is largely because of the lack of and inadequacy of services and also women's lack of awareness of their rights to use the services. Effective access to these services is critical not only to support women but also provide options to escape violence and abuse and contribute to the overall development of the country, for generations to come. The Government of Kiribati has shown commitment to address gender issues."
